pg007_n0008: In this chapter, you will learn about health principles.
pg007_n0009: These include eating a balanced diet, doing physical exercises and maintaining both personal and environmental cleanliness.
pg007_n0010: However, you will also explore safety signs and other important health information in the environment.

pg007_n0012: You will also be able to protect your health and the health of others.

pg008_n0009: A balanced diet is a meal with all the food nutrients in the correct proportions.
pg008_n0010: It is made up of foods from three main groups.
pg008_n0011: The groups are energy-giving foods, body-building foods, protective foods.
pg008_n0012: Energy-giving foods have carbohydrate and fat nutrients.
pg008_n0014: Protective foods have vitamins and minerals nutrients.
pg008_n0015: Eating a balanced diet helps make the body’s immune system strong to fight off diseases.

pg009_n0010: Carbohydrate-rich foods are maize, potatoes, cassava, bananas, rice and bread.
pg009_n0011: Foods rich in fats include coconut, peanuts, sunflower seeds and avocados.
pg009_n0012: These foods provide the energy needed for daily activities like playing, farming and walking.
pg009_n0013: Fats also help keep the body warm.

pg010_n0021: Also, they help build and strengthen the body’s muscles and bones.

pg011_n0011: But, water is not a main food group in a balanced diet.

pg011_n0013: It helps in the process of breaking down food in the digestive system.
pg011_n0014: Also, water regulates body temperature and helps in nutrient absorption.
pg011_n0015: It also helps remove waste and harmful substances from the body.

pg012_n0002: Balanced diet for different groups of people
pg012_n0004: Nutritional needs are different for each group of people.
pg012_n0005: These groups are based on age, like children, adolescents and the elderly.
pg012_n0006: Also, it depend on work people do, like manual workers, and health status, like the sick.
pg012_n0010: Children need foods rich in protein because they are growing.
pg012_n0011: These foods include milk, meat, fish, beans, peas, lentils and eggs.
pg012_n0012: These foods help build the body, strengthen the immune system and support brain development.
pg012_n0013: Children also need energy-giving foods to provide strength needed for doing activities like playing.
pg012_n0014: Protective foods are needed to make their immune system strong.

pg013_n0004: During adolescence, the body grows fast and goes through changes.
pg013_n0005: Adolescents need a diet rich in body-building, protective and energy-giving foods.
pg013_n0006: At this age, they are involved in many activities like sports, farming and studying for long hours.
pg013_n0007: Because of this, their diet should include plenty of energy-giving foods to provide enough energy for these activities.

pg013_n0020: A small amount of energy-giving foods is needed to support light activities.

pg013_n0022: Body-building foods are also important to replace old or damaged cells.

pg014_n0010: Manual workers need a large amount of energy-giving foods.

pg017_n0049: Maintaining hygiene of the body and the environment is important for good health.
pg017_n0050: Body and environment must be kept clean all the time.
pg018_n0004: Personal hygiene is important for our health.
pg018_n0005: The body and clothes should be cleaned using proper tools to avoid diseases.
pg018_n0006: Personal hygiene includes cleaning the mouth, skin, hair, nails and clothes.
pg018_n0010: The mouth should be cleaned using a toothbrush, toothpaste, and clean, safe water.
pg018_n0011: Brushing removes food particles from the teeth.
pg018_n0012: If the food particles remain, bacteria in the mouth feed on them and produce acid.
pg018_n0013: This acid damages the teeth and causes cavities.
pg018_n0014: It is important to brush your teeth at least twice a day.
pg018_n0015: Brush your teeth in the morning when you wake up and at night before going to bed.
pg018_n0016: This helps keep your teeth healthy.

pg018_n0020: Clean water and soap should be used for bathing.
pg018_n0021: It is good to bathe every day, in the morning and evening to avoid skin diseases.
pg018_n0022: If we do not bathe, our bodies can smell bad.
pg018_n0023: After bathing, dry the body with a clean towel.
pg018_n0024: Apply body oil to keep the skin soft and prevent it from drying.
pg018_n0025: We should also wash our faces with clean water and soap after waking up.
pg018_n0026: This helps remove rheum and prevent eye diseases.

pg019_n0010: Hair should be cared for by regularly washing with clean water and soap.
pg019_n0011: It is also important to care the hair by braiding, shaving or combing to look clean and neat.
pg019_n0012: Keeping hair clean helps prevent dandruff and pests like lice.
pg019_n0013: This also helps prevent scalp infections such as ringworms.
pg019_n0017: Fingernails and toenails should be kept short and clean by cutting them regularly.
pg019_n0018: Long nails can hold dirt with germs that cause diseases.
pg019_n0019: Washing hands and nails with clean running water and soap helps remove these germs.
pg019_n0023: Clothes should be washed with clean water and soap to remove dirt.
pg019_n0024: Wearing dirty clothes can cause body odour and lead to skin problems like itching and rashes.
pg019_n0025: After washing, clothes should be properly dried and ironed.
pg019_n0026: Ironing helps kill germs and keeps the clothes looking neat.

pg032_n0014: The effects of diseases on human health
pg032_n0018: Disease is an abnormal condition or disorders in a living organism that disrupts normal functioning of the body.
pg032_n0019: Many diseases are caused by germs found in our surroundings.
pg032_n0020: These germs are found in air, soil, water, unsafe food and animal bodily fluids like blood.
pg032_n0021: Germs can enter the body through eating contaminated food, drinking unsafe water, breathing in contaminated air, or touching an infected person.
pg032_n0022: However, some diseases are not caused by germs, such as hereditary diseases.

pg033_n0013: There are different types of diseases that affect the human body.
pg033_n0014: These diseases are grouped into two main types namely: communicable diseases and non-communicable diseases.

pg033_n0018: Communicable diseases are illnesses that spread from one person to another.
pg033_n0019: These diseases are caused by pathogens like bacteria and viruses.
pg033_n0020: Examples of communicable diseases are malaria, cholera, chickenpox, tuberculosis, hepatitis and Corona Virus Disease of 2019 (COVID-19).
pg033_n0024: Malaria is a disease caused by parasites called plasmodium.
pg033_n0025: The disease is spread by a female mosquito called Anopheles.
pg034_n0002: The mosquito transmits malaria by injecting the parasites into the human body when it bites a person.

pg035_n0004: Malaria can be controlled by destroying places where mosquitoes breed.
pg035_n0005: These places include bushes, long grass, and stagnant water in puddles.
pg035_n0006: Tyres, coconut shells and cans that hold water can also serve as breeding areas for mosquitoes.
pg035_n0007: Kerosene or larvicide can be spread on puddles to kill mosquito larvae.
pg035_n0008: Also, coconut shells and other breeding areas should be destroyed.
pg035_n0009: Malaria can also be prevented by sleeping under a treated mosquito net.
pg035_n0010: Other ways include using mosquito sprays, coils and repellents.
pg035_n0011: Also, putting wire mesh on windows and doors to prevent mosquitoes from entering the house.
pg035_n0012: If someone has malaria symptoms, they should go to the hospital for diagnosis and treatment.

pg135_n0004: Program control structures refer to how the flow of computer instructions is managed.
pg135_n0005: There are three types of program control structures namely sequence, repetition and selection.
pg135_n0009: In programming, a sequence structure follows the order of flow of instructions or blocks from top to bottom.
pg135_n0010: The first block is executed before the next block.

pg007_n0007_easy_read: Good health is important for our well-being.
pg007_n0008_easy_read: In this chapter, you will learn about health principles.
pg007_n0009_easy_read:
Health principles include:
- eating a balanced diet
- doing physical exercise
- keeping yourself clean
- keeping the environment clean
pg007_n0010_easy_read: You will also learn about safety signs and other important health information in the environment.
pg007_n0011_easy_read: The skills you develop will help you follow health principles.
pg007_n0012_easy_read: You will also be able to protect your health and the health of other people.
pg007_n0014_easy_read: Things you can do every day to take care of your health
pg007_n0018_easy_read: Following health principles is important to stay healthy.
pg007_n0019_easy_read: Good health means being strong in body and mind.
pg007_n0020_easy_read:
To be healthy, you need to:
- eat a balanced diet
- do physical exercise regularly
- keep yourself clean
- keep the environment clean
pg007_n0021_easy_read: It is also important to follow safety signs and health information in the environment.
pg007_n0022_easy_read: Figure 1 shows examples of health principles.
pg008_n0024_easy_read: 1. Use the library or reliable online sources to learn about health principles.
pg008_n0026_easy_read: 2. Share what you find with other pupils in the class for discussion.
pg008_n0009_easy_read: A balanced diet is a meal with all the food nutrients in the right amounts.
pg008_n0010_easy_read: A balanced diet is made up of foods from 3 main groups.
pg008_n0011_easy_read:
The 3 groups are:
- energy-giving foods
- body-building foods
- protective foods
pg008_n0012_easy_read: Energy-giving foods have carbohydrate and fat nutrients.
pg008_n0014_easy_read: Protective foods have vitamin and mineral nutrients.
pg008_n0015_easy_read:
Eating a balanced diet helps make the body’s immune system strong.
This helps the body fight diseases.
pg008_n0016_easy_read: Figure 2 shows examples of the main food groups in a balanced diet.

- body-building foods
- protective foods
pg009_n0009_easy_read: Foods that give the body energy include foods rich in carbohydrates and fats.
pg009_n0010_easy_read:
Foods rich in carbohydrates are:
- maize
- potatoes
- cassava
- bananas
- rice
- bread
pg009_n0011_easy_read:
Foods rich in fats include:
- coconut
- peanuts
- sunflower seeds
- avocados
pg009_n0012_easy_read:
These foods give the body the energy it needs for daily activities such as:
- playing
- farming
- walking
pg009_n0013_easy_read: Fats also help keep the body warm.
